content:
Formula: Shannon Information Entropy
Exact Expression: H(X) = -\sum_{x \in \mathcal{X}} P(x) \log_2 P(x)
Definitions: Fundamental measure of the average rate at which information is produced by a stochastic source of data.
Derivation/Reference: Claude E. Shannon, A Mathematical Theory of Communication (Bell System Technical Journal, 1948)
Example: Fair coin toss: P(H)=P(T)=0.5 -> H = -(0.5*log2(0.5) + 0.5*log2(0.5)) = -(-0.5 - 0.5) = 1.0 bit
Domain: information_theory
Assumptions: P(x) >= 0, sum P(x) = 1, with 0 * log(0) = 0 by continuity
Common Errors: Using natural log ln instead of log2 without converting units to nats
subject: Shannon Information Entropy
